hook: Merging Inter with school could hit *85%* local seats, BRS claims
hook_b: Merging Inter with school could hit *85%* local seats, BRS claims
tldr: BRS MLC Dasoju Sravan Kumar wrote to CM Revanth Reddy alleging that merging Intermediate with school education would let out-of-state students gain local status.

beats.what: He says if Classes 9-12 become one senior secondary school, corporate colleges could sell four-year Hyderabad hostel packages that make outside students 'local'.
beats.why: Today many students from AP and other states come to Hyderabad only for two Intermediate years, so they count as non-local.
beats.care: If you or a sibling are aiming for MBBS or engineering seats in Telangana, the 85% local quota is what this argument is about.

causes.label: Plan to merge Inter with school

event.label: BRS letter to CM on local status

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: He also says there is no clarity on which board would conduct exams if Classes 9-12 are merged.

cards.q: Should Classes 9 to 12 become one senior secondary school in Telangana?

qs: How many out-of-state students join Hyderabad colleges only for Intermediate?
Which board would set exams if Classes 9-12 merge?

facts.t: Local status depends on *four* continuous years of study before the entrance exam.

viz.verdict: BRS says merged schooling could change who qualifies; the state hasn't replied in this report

steps.e: Classes 9-12 as one senior secondary school

viz.verdict: Two boards today, one system proposed

learn.t: Local status = eligibility for state-reserved seats, based on 4 years of study before the entrance exam

watch: The report carries no government reply; watch for which board would run exams under any merged system.

sources.name: Siasat
sources.title: Scrapping Inter may cost Telangana students local status, says BRS

fact: BRS says scrapping Inter could let outsiders claim Telangana's *85%* local seats
twist: Local status is set by where you studied the four years before the entrance exam, not where you were born.
